results.title: 7 Types of Complaints From Customers (Plus How To Resolve Them) | Indeed.com
results.content: A customer may make a complaint if they have problems with a company's product or service. For example, a customer may explain that a product arrived broken or that the product functions differently than they expected. When this happens, it's important to document the customer's concerns thoroughly. This documentation can help your company determine whether to change its products or services to improve the quality.After documenting the complaint, ask questions to determine the source of the problem. You can ask the customer to show you the problem with the product to ensure they're using it correctly. If they're misusing the product, you can politely show them how to use it correctly to meet their needs. If the product is broken, most companies have policies to replace the item at no cost [...] A personnel complaint may occur when a customer feels unhappy about their interaction with someone in the company. If a customer makes a personnel complaint, ask the customer to describe their interaction with the employee. If they're unsure of the name of the employee, ask them to provide a description of the person based on their interaction or conversation. Acknowledge the customer's frustration and apologize to them for the situation. Let them know you plan to speak with the employee about the issue.If you're a customer service representative, you can let your manager know about the complaint so they can speak with the employee about the interaction. If you're a manager, have an honest conversation with the employee to understand the situation from their point of view. You can arrange [...] Delivery complaints may occur when a company changes the expected delivery date of a product. It's common for online businesses, which ship their products to customers in the mail. Sometimes, the mail carrier may be the cause of the delivery delay, rather than the business. When this happens, you can look up the tracking details for the package and assure the customer it's on the way to them. If you notice the carrier may have lost the package, make sure to get in touch with the carrier to resolve the issue.If the business causes the delivery change or delay, apologize to the customer for the inconvenience. Explain why the business may have shipped the package later than expected. For example, if you had an influx of orders over the holiday season, tell the customer you had more orders

results.title: Different types of customer feedback (and what to do with them)
results.content:
With negative ones, ask to discuss it further. You may be able to resolve whatever triggered the bad review. Brownie points if you go back and let whoever complained know when you’ve fixed the issues.

### Social media mentions

Customers don’t always come to you with feedback. Sometimes they share it where their friends and followers can see. Posts on X, LinkedIn, and Reddit all count. TikTok comments and YouTube replies do too.

A frustrated customer might post about a feature that’s broken. A delighted one might post a workflow they built with your product. Both are useful signals you’d never see in a survey.

results.title: Customer Complaints: 12 Examples and How to Handl...
results.content:
#### How can businesses reduce customer complaints?

Reduce complaints by removing the friction that causes them: faster response times, a searchable knowledge base for self-service, and clear communication about timelines and policies. Tracking recurring complaints also matters, and tools like Featurebase let you group feedback by theme so you can fix root causes before they generate more tickets.

#### What is the best way to respond to an angry customer complaint?

Acknowledge the issue and take responsibility where you fell short, empathize with the frustration, and move quickly to a concrete solution with a clear timeline. Staying calm and honest matters more than being clever, and following up afterward turns a rough moment into a loyal customer. [...] ### 6. Late, wrong, or damaged deliveries

"The tracking says delivered, but nothing arrived." Delivery issues spike during busy seasons and are often outside your direct control, which makes them tricky.

How to handle it: Track the package yourself before asking the customer to do anything. If it is genuinely lost or wrong, arrange a replacement and a return, and offer a small goodwill gesture for the inconvenience. Keep the customer updated rather than going silent.

### 7. An item is out of stock

"I finally decided to buy and now it's gone." Out-of-stock complaints are time-sensitive, and the frustration grows the longer an item is unavailable. [...] ## Best practices for handling any customer complaint

The examples differ, but a reliable response follows the same 4 steps no matter the complaint:

 Acknowledge: Confirm you understand the issue and, where you fell short, own it. People want to feel heard before they hear a solution.
 Empathize: Show you get why they are frustrated. A little warmth de-escalates far more than a scripted apology.
 Solve: Offer a concrete fix, or the closest thing you can do, with clear timelines you will actually meet.
 Follow up: Check back to confirm the issue is truly resolved. This is the step most teams skip, and the one customers remember.

Lead with honesty throughout. Sugarcoating or over-promising only drags the interaction out and erodes trust.

results.title: How to Handle Customer Complaints: A Guide for Small Businesses | CO- by US Chamber of Commerce
results.content:
The most common customer complaints include:

 Long wait times during customer service calls.
 A staff member or another customer offended them.
 Out-of-stock or discontinued products.
 Defective or unacceptable goods or services.
 Items were missing or broken during shipping.
 Inadequate communication about staff turnover or policy changes.
 Your goods or services didn’t meet their expectations.
 A concern about billing or fees.

Check in with customers who reported problems or left negative business reviews. Thank them for reaching out, confirm they’re satisfied with the resolution, and listen to any additional feedback they provide.
